summary: Runner study: 85 closed paper trades, average -6.6% (median -20.1%, 14% won, -8.7% without the single best trade).
Risk rules: Listed (-4.3%) and dropped (-10.8%) coins did about the same so far.

Numbers that reliably separated winners from losers (luck-corrected): 24h change over 100% (+416172.1% against +159.7%); 24h change under 25% (-15.5% against +201221.3%); Hour of day (UTC) 12-18 (+375897.5% against +164.3%).
Against random coins: The runners list (-4.3%) and random coins (+128241.1%) did about the same so far.
Locked test (from 2026-10-25): 7 rules found, but only 0 trades closed since the lock date. Too few to judge.
Week by week: 24h change over 100% pointed the same way in 2 of 2 weeks; 24h change under 25% pointed the same way in 2 of 2 weeks.

Risk: at 10% of the account per trade the listed runners had a worst drawdown of 28.2% and a longest losing run of 20. A size of about 7.4% per trade would keep 22 losses in a row under a 30% account hit.
Progress: 85 of 30 closed trades needed before reading results (0 to go).
notes: Returns are paper returns after 3% entry slippage plus the price impact of a $1,000 order on the pool liquidity. They ignore gas, exit liquidity and rugs, so real results would be lower. One huge winner can lift an average, so the median and the average without the best trade are shown.
